purpose: Capture the actual Windows child startup/readiness error on the next existing native test run without changing readiness, timeout-under-test, or production containment.
failure_sequence: The existing 30-second timeout has already returned Err. Retain that original Elapsed value for the final panic.
Capture wrapper.id and wrapper.try_wait Result, including any io::Error; inspect the PID file length and ready-file try_exists Result independently.
Read no more than 129 PID-file bytes; retain a numeric PID only when UTF-8 parsing succeeds, report trimmed_nonempty, and mark oversized/invalid input without dumping arbitrary file contents.
Take existing stdout/stderr pipe handles only in this Err branch. No stream is read or reconfigured on the successful path.
Drop the original process_tree guard and wrapper before reading output. This invokes the existing cleanup behavior rather than adding a new containment implementation.

Drain both detached read handles concurrently against the same 250-millisecond Tokio deadline. Retain at most 4096 bytes per stream and read one extra byte to distinguish exact-limit EOF from truncation.

Always panic with the original readiness error plus diagnostic status. Read errors, missing pipes, truncation, and diagnostic deadline expiry explicitly say incomplete; only observed EOF says complete_eof.

bounds.output_rendering: Retained bytes are rendered as debug-escaped String::from_utf8_lossy output; this is bounded startup diagnostics, not a byte-perfect full-stream archive.
bounds.timing_scope: The 250ms shared Tokio deadline bounds only the post-cleanup asynchronous pipe-read stage. Local PID/metadata/try_wait syscalls and OS scheduling are not a hard real-time bound; no readiness or tested timeout is extended.

prepared_tests_not_run.name: readiness_output_distinguishes_exact_limit_from_truncation
prepared_tests_not_run.coverage: 0 bytes, exactly 4096 bytes with observed EOF, and 4097 bytes with explicit truncation.

prepared_tests_not_run.name: readiness_output_preserves_partial_bytes_on_shared_deadline
prepared_tests_not_run.coverage: A partial stream that remains pending does not erase its prefix or prevent the other stream from completing under the shared deadline.

prepared_tests_not_run.name: readiness_output_preserves_read_error_and_missing_pipe
prepared_tests_not_run.coverage: Preserve the partial prefix and concrete read error; missing pipe is explicitly incomplete.

single_followup_snapshot_in_this_prepara.direct_job_fetch_endpoint: github_fetch rejected the direct /actions/jobs URL as an unsupported endpoint; no bypass attempted. The purpose-built run-jobs tool supplied the snapshot.

limitations: No Windows native execution or Rust compilation was performed. This candidate does not establish or repair the underlying startup cause.

Backpressure on the normal path is deliberately unchanged; if a full pipe caused the original readiness failure, the next failure will retain a bounded prefix rather than silently removing that condition.
Taking and draining output only after failure cannot provide a live child-process status beyond the captured wrapper exit and written child PID.
If a descendant still holds a pipe open after existing cleanup, the shared read deadline returns an incomplete diagnostic rather than waiting indefinitely.
Root must perform the canonical formatter and rely on real CI compilation/testing before treating the candidate as validated.
